title: Korea Meteorological Administration — yellow dust (Asian dust) action guide and information
claims: The main source regions affecting Korea are the Gobi Desert and Inner Mongolian Plateau; about 50% arrive directly from the Gobi/Inner Mongolia region, 14% via the northeast China desert zone and 17% via the Loess Plateau, so Gobi/Inner Mongolia-origin dust accounts for about 81%.

A yellow dust alert is issued when PM10 at or above 800 µg/m3 is expected to persist for at least two hours; on a dust day, KMA advises wearing a mask and protective glasses outdoors, closing windows, and keeping the elderly and people with respiratory conditions indoors.

Yellow dust particles are typically 1–10 µm soil particles, distinct from fine dust (PM10/PM2.5, mostly carbon or ions); KMA handles yellow dust while the Ministry of Environment handles fine dust forecasts.
